questions.q: What does mongostat show, and what's the closest analogy this lesson gives for it?
options: Continuously updating server-wide operation counters, memory, and connections — genuinely comparable to running top against the database process
A one-time snapshot of disk usage, comparable to running du
A GUI-only dashboard with no command-line equivalent
A tool exclusive to MongoDB Atlas, unavailable for self-managed deployments
questions.explain: mongostat is a CLI tool that polls mongod and prints continuously updating real-time stats, compared to top for MongoDB.

questions.q: What question does mongotop answer that mongostat doesn't?
options: Which specific collection is consuming read/write time, not just how busy the server is overall
How much disk space each database is using
Which users are currently authenticated
What the server's uptime has been since last restart
questions.explain: mongotop breaks read/write time down per collection, narrowing a server-wide spike to its specific source.

questions.q: What does MongoDB Atlas provide that the mongostat/mongotop CLI tools don't, per this lesson?
options: Historical retention of these metrics, configurable alerting, and a Performance Advisor that recommends indexes
Nothing — Atlas dashboards show strictly less information than the CLI tools
Atlas can only show data for the current second, with no additional features
Atlas replaces the need for indexes entirely
questions.explain: Atlas dashboards cover the same metric categories but add historical trends, alerting, and Performance Advisor's index recommendations.

questions.q: What does Atlas's Performance Advisor do?
options: Actively analyzes slow operations and recommends indexes
Automatically backs up the database every hour
Encrypts data at rest without any configuration
Replaces the need for authentication
questions.explain: Performance Advisor goes beyond raw monitoring into tuning guidance, analyzing slow operations to recommend indexes.

questions.q: Per this lesson, why would a team still use mongostat/mongotop even if they have Atlas dashboards?
options: They're useful in the moment during an active incident when already at a terminal, and are what self-managed deployments rely on directly
Atlas dashboards cannot be accessed by anyone but administrators
mongostat and mongotop are strictly faster than Atlas in every scenario
Atlas does not support any form of real-time monitoring
questions.explain: The CLI tools remain the go-to for self-managed deployments and for in-the-moment terminal-based incident response, complementing rather than being replaced by Atlas.
